headword: {西南戦争|せいなんせんそう}

definitions.gloss: the Satsuma Rebellion of 1877, led by Saigō Takamori
definitions.explanation: The rebellion of former samurai from Satsuma (now Kagoshima) against the new Meiji government in 1877, led by Saigō Takamori. Government conscript troops defeated them after months of fighting, including the siege of Kumamoto Castle, and Saigō died at Shiroyama. It was the last civil war in Japan.

examples.english: After the Satsuma Rebellion, there were no more armed uprisings of former samurai against the government.

notes:
{西南|せいなん} (southwest) refers to Kyushu, where the fighting took place. In English it is usually called the Satsuma Rebellion; {西南|せいなん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{役|えき} is an older name.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The war marked the end of the samurai as a class and the victory of the conscript army. Saigō, though he died a rebel, became a popular hero; his statue stands in Ueno Park in Tokyo.
